Minimum Coin Change using Dynamic Programming You are given an unlimited supply of coins of different denominations and a target amount. Your task is to determine the minimum number of coins required to make the target amount exactly. If it is not possible to form the target amount, the algorithm should report that no solution exists. A common Dynamic Programming approach solves this problem by computing the minimum number of coins required for all smaller amounts before calculating the answer for the target amount. Which of the following statements is NOT true about solving the Minimum Coin Change problem using Dynamic Programming?
options: We can define each subproblem as finding the minimum number of coins required to make every amount from 0 up to the target amount.
The minimum number of coins required for a larger amount can be computed using the optimal solutions already obtained for smaller amounts.
A Dynamic Programming solution stores the minimum number of coins required for each intermediate amount so that these values can be reused instead of being recomputed.

The order in which the Dynamic Programming table is filled (for example, solving larger amounts before smaller ones without already having their answers) does not affect the correctness of the algorithm.
questions.correct_answer: The order in which the Dynamic Programming table is filled (for example, solving larger amounts before smaller ones without already having their answers) does not affect the correctness of the algorithm.
